extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed final mechanism ontology from article text, figures, S1 Fig/S1 Video inventory, and methods.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Hst 5, P113, HHP1, di-PH2, di-WP2, di-18Hc
mechanism_claims.claim_text: Laminarin inhibition supports binding of tested peptides to beta-1,3-glucan cell-wall component as an early interaction relevant to candidacidal activity.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=17:3.4 Binding of Hybrid Peptides to the Cell Surface of C. albicans via a Specific Interaction with β-1,3-Glucan; xml:fig=2:Fig 2

mechanism_claims.limitations: Binding inhibition is qualitative/figure-based and is not converted into exact potency values.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: CD spectra show environment-dependent secondary structure differences, with HHP1 more alpha-helical in TFE and di-18Hc/di-PH2 showing moderate helical folding in laminarin.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Secondary structure supports interaction context but is not alone a direct killing mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Killing kinetics separate membrane-attacking fast killers (di-WP2 and di-18Hc) from slower translocating peptides such as di-PH2, while HHP1 shows fast killing despite cytosolic localization.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Figure curves are not digitized; only source-supported qualitative kinetic conclusions are recorded.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: FITC-labeled Hst 5, P113, HHP1, di-PH2, di-WP2, di-18Hc
mechanism_claims.claim_text: Confocal microscopy localizes Hst 5, P113, HHP1, and di-PH2 into cytoplasm, while di-WP2 accumulates mainly at the cell surface with PI uptake similar to di-18Hc.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=20:3.7 Localization of Hst 5, P113, di-18Hc and Hybrids Peptides during C. albicans Killing; xml:fig=5:Fig 5; supp:S1 Video

mechanism_claims.limitations: S1 Video was present locally but not quantitatively parsed; mechanism conclusion is based on article text/figure caption.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Hst 5, P113, HHP1, di-PH2, di-WP2, di-18Hc
mechanism_claims.claim_text: Energy depletion by sodium azide blocks translocation/PI influx for Hst 5, P113, di-PH2, and HHP1 but not di-WP2/di-18Hc surface binding and PI uptake, supporting different uptake/death routes.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=21:3.8 Candidacidal Activities of Membrane Attacking Peptides Are Not Affected by Energy Depletion; xml:fig=6:Fig 6

mechanism_claims.limitations: The figure is interpreted qualitatively; no exact curve values were extracted.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Hst 5, P113, HHP1, di-PH2, di-WP2, di-18Hc
mechanism_claims.claim_text: ROS increases are observed for Hst 5, P113, and di-PH2, but ascorbic-acid reduction of ROS does not reduce candidacidal activity, so ROS is not promoted as the main killing event.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Preserves the paper's caveat that ROS production is likely secondary/contextual rather than a major antimicrobial mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper proposes the C-terminal KFH motif as important for cytosolic translocation of hybrid peptides, but frames this as an inference requiring further research.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Do not upgrade KFH motif explanation to a direct mechanism; local S1 Fig is image-only and supports localization context only.
